stories.headline: Babiš floats selling state explosives maker Explosia, drawing sharp opposition backlash
stories.summary: Prime Minister Babiš said during a visit to Explosia's Pardubice facility that the state is considering selling the strategic explosives and ammunition manufacturer — maker of Semtex — citing its current valuation of 15-20 billion CZK. He confirmed France expressed interest via President Macron. Opposition figures and security experts attacked the proposal as dangerous and contradictory given Babiš previously insisted Explosia was a strategic asset. Finance Minister Schillerová said the sale remains a commercial idea only, with price as the sole criterion.

stories.headline: Sudeten German congress in Brno ignites Czech-German relations controversy and coalition rift
stories.summary: The 76th Sudeten German Congress held in Brno for the first time in Czech history became a major political flashpoint. SPD leader Okamura campaigned against the congress and pushed a parliamentary resolution urging organisers to cancel; ANO largely abstained. President Pavel met Bavarian PM Söder on the sidelines, while Finance Minister Schillerová refused to meet Söder separately, citing an inflamed atmosphere. Czech writer Milan Uhde received the Sudeten Germans' highest award. The episode strained Czech-Bavarian and broader Czech-German relations, with German media and EU partners critical of the coalition's posture.

stories.headline: President Pavel calls on NATO to 'show its teeth' against Russia at GLOBSEC in Prague
stories.summary: At the GLOBSEC security forum hosted in Prague on 21–22 May, President Pavel delivered a high-profile speech urging NATO allies to respond decisively to Russian provocations on the Alliance's eastern flank, proposing options including shooting down Russian aircraft violating NATO airspace, disconnecting Russia from the internet, and cutting off its banks from global financial systems. Pavel also argued that supporting Ukraine is not charity but a security investment, and warned against a 'bad peace.' The speech received wide international coverage and drew criticism from PM Babiš's camp domestically.

stories.headline: ANO sidelines SPD in Chief of General Staff appointment, fuelling coalition tensions over defense ministry
stories.summary: A significant coalition rift emerged after PM Babiš bypassed SPD's defense minister Jaromír Zůna to appoint Miroslav Hlaváč as new Chief of the General Staff — overriding all four candidates Zůna had proposed. Zůna was the only cabinet member to vote against. Reports described repeated tense meetings between Babiš and Zůna over army reform concepts, and the appointment of Jakub Landovský as government envoy for NATO commitments without consulting SPD. Opposition figures including ODS euroMP Vondra called for Zůna's resignation; SPD defended the minister. Babiš was described as increasingly asserting direct control over defence policy.

stories.headline: CNB Governor Michl signals rate hikes possible, clashes with Babiš government over fiscal policy
stories.summary: CNB Governor Aleš Michl gave an unusually combative interview in the Insider podcast declaring he is willing to 'crush the economy' to prevent inflation from rising, and that the era of low interest rates is permanently over. Multiple Czech outlets criticised this posture as inconsistent with his past dovish record. Michl also explicitly criticised the Babiš government's high fiscal deficits as incompatible with a low-rate environment and rejected government pressure for cheaper mortgages. Bloomberg and international analysts flagged that the CNB is holding rates at 3.5% while signalling upward bias if core inflation risks emerge. The Czech Republic also revised economic growth forecasts downward alongside the EU.

stories.headline: Babiš-Pavel standoff deepens over NATO Ankara summit delegation
stories.summary: The ongoing constitutional dispute between President Pavel and PM Babiš over who may attend the July NATO summit in Ankara as part of the official Czech delegation came to a head this week. Babiš has insisted the president cannot be part of the government delegation, while Pavel argues he has traditionally represented the country at summits and even offered to self-fund his attendance. Politico described a rocky relationship with repeated clashes over foreign policy, democratic norms and business conflicts of interest. Foreign Minister Macinka proposed delaying the decision until after the 12 June NATO defence ministers' meeting.

stories.headline: Czech army chief says Ukraine joining NATO is a 'logical step'
stories.summary: Chief of the Czech Armed Forces General Karel Řehka, speaking at GLOBSEC in Prague, stated that Ukraine's accession to NATO is the next logical step for European security, describing Ukraine as a security provider as well as consumer. Řehka also urged the Czech Republic to increase defence spending to well above 2% of GDP, which put him in tension with the Babiš government's fiscal approach.

stories.headline: Babiš government refuses Ukraine military aid funding, drawing NATO criticism
stories.summary: PM Babiš has maintained since autumn 2025 that no Czech state budget funds will go to weapons for Ukraine. This week, NATO Secretary General Rutte publicly criticised allies including — by description — the Czech Republic for insufficient Ukraine support. Czech commentary described the government seeking 'accounting tricks' to show 2% GDP defence spending on paper without real rearmament. The Czech Republic's position contrasted sharply with statements by the army chief and president.
